architecture_audit_answers.q1_explicit_temporal_modeling: No — rows are i.i.d. to HGB; horizon_hour is a scalar feature, not a sequence position.
architecture_audit_answers.q2_explicit_horizon_dependencies: No — no coupling mechanism between predictions at different horizons of the same origin.
architecture_audit_answers.q3_shared_representation_across_horizons: Only implicit parameter sharing via one global tree ensemble; no explicit multi-task structure.
architecture_audit_answers.q4_exploits_sequential_trajectory: No — despite strong measured autocorrelation (0.67-0.93) in horizon-varying NWP inputs within an origin, no neighbor-horizon deltas/trends are exposed or modeled explicitly.
architecture_audit_answers.q5_h9_h12_from_tabular_limitation: Plausible but confounded — H9-H12 error peak co-locates with the diurnal peak in solar elevation/clearsky GHI, i.e. largest physical magnitude, so this is not proof of an architectural cause; it motivates the hypothesis without confirming it.
architecture_audit_answers.q6_information_already_encoded: Trailing-24h observation summary stats, last obs, per-horizon NWP forecast fields, LWP/IWP, clearsky GHI (raw + terrain-adjusted), solar geometry, terrain obstruction, three prior-stage model predictions plus disagreement.
architecture_audit_answers.q7_missing_architectural_capability: (a) neighbor-horizon/sequence coupling, (b) explicit shared multi-task representation across an origin's 24 horizons, (c) as a non-coupling alternative, a dedicated residual-modeling second stage.

candidates.name: Temporal sequence model (per-origin trajectory encoder)
candidates.information_used: 24-step per-origin sequence of horizon-varying features + static ctx_* vector; all pre-existing columns reshaped, no new data
candidates.why_could_improve_h9_h12: Small GRU/TCN can exploit measured trajectory momentum (autocorr 0.67-0.93) that HGB does not use explicitly
candidates.why_different_from_phase9: Phase 9 candidates added single features to the same row-independent HGB; this changes the processing architecture itself
candidates.overfitting_risk: Highest of the three — only 173 EVEN origins for a sequence NN
candidates.computational_cost: Low-moderate; CPU-trainable in minutes but needs careful regularization

candidates.name: Multi-horizon shared-representation model
candidates.hgb_limitation_addressed: No shared multi-task representation across H1-H24 of one origin (audit q2, q3)
candidates.information_used: Same 37 features; joint multi-task training over all 24 horizons per origin instead of independent row fits
candidates.why_could_improve_h9_h12: Lets the model borrow strength across an origin's horizons if H9-H12 errors are structurally linked to an origin-level regime rather than purely independent per-row noise
candidates.why_different_from_phase9: Changes what is jointly optimized, not what features exist — distinct from both Phase 9 feature-engineering candidates and from Candidate A's recurrence-based coupling
candidates.overfitting_risk: Moderate — smaller than Candidate A since no recurrent state, but still risk of per-origin idiosyncrasy overfit with only 173 EVEN origins
candidates.computational_cost: Low; small MLP, seconds to low minutes on CPU

candidates.name: Residual/dual-stage architecture
candidates.hgb_limitation_addressed: None directly — tests whether a second learned stage recovers residual structure the single-stage tabular model misses (audit q7c)
candidates.information_used: Stage 1: same-pipeline reconstructed HGB control (explicitly labeled, per Phase 9 caveat). Stage 2: trained on Stage 1's OOF residuals using same 37 features plus intrinsic within-origin residual-context derivations
candidates.why_could_improve_h9_h12: If Stage 1 residuals at H9-H12 have exploitable conditional structure a single HGB fit under-fits
candidates.why_different_from_phase9: Phase 9's disagreement-signal candidate was one new feature fed into the same one-stage model; this is a separately trained second stage
candidates.overfitting_risk: Lowest of the three, but weakest link to the audited architectural gap; closest in spirit to the already gate-failed Phase 9 Candidate 3/A
candidates.evaluation: Stage 1 via 5-fold OOF-by-origin; Stage 2 trained only on Stage 1's out-of-fold residuals, validated with its own 5-fold OOF-by-origin

ranking.reason: Most directly targets best-evidenced architectural gap; lower overfitting risk than A given dataset size; cheap and easy to keep leakage-safe

selected_primary_architecture.name: Multi-horizon shared-representation model
selected_primary_architecture.output_structure: Shared small MLP trunk (<=2 hidden layers, width <=64, dropout) + horizon embedding, multi-task loss batched per origin (all 24 horizons jointly), one predicted SW_IN per (origin, horizon)

training_procedure.batching: grouped by origin (24 rows per group)
training_procedure.loss: MAE averaged over the 24 horizons per origin
training_procedure.regularization: dropout + weight decay, deliberately small/fixed configuration, no hyperparameter sweep

validation_procedure.scheme: 5-fold OOF, folds assigned by origin_id, all 24 horizons of an origin kept in one fold
validation_procedure.control: same-pipeline reconstructed HGB control (explicitly labeled as reconstructed, not official champion), same EVEN OOF folds

leakage_controls: EVEN only; ODD not read or referenced
no future actual SW_IN or future errors as inputs
architecture/hyperparameters fixed before any OOF result is inspected

preregistered_gates.G1: aggregated delta_mae <= -0.50 W/m^2 vs EVEN same-pipeline control
preregistered_gates.G4: candidate nMAE <= control nMAE AND candidate RMSE <= control RMSE
preregistered_gates.G6: exact control reproduction reported honestly as approximate unless original Stage 8.1 code/hyperparameters are located; official champion numbers never replaced

selected_primary_architecture.scientific_justification: Smallest, lowest-risk architectural change directly targeting a concretely demonstrated gap (no shared/multi-task representation across an origin's 24 horizons); reuses 100% of existing feature space; no new hyperparameter sweep; cleanly answers whether cross-horizon shared representation extracts more signal than fully independent tabular treatment, without touching ODD or reopening feature research.

explicit_non_claims: Not claimed that Candidate B will pass its gates.
Not claimed H9-H12 error is caused by architecture rather than input-magnitude/physical volatility.
Not claimed 28.0688% nMAE is a lower bound.
Not claimed neural/temporal architectures cannot help in some other form in the future.
